mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,300,000 signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST < 1300.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase above 0.4 percentage points from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.4pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during two consecutive months of UNRATE > 0.4pp increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during three consecutive months of INDPRO < -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which increases uncertainty and risk premiums, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during four consecutive months of RSAFS < -1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their prior month values signals a labor market expansion with rising participation and stable unemployment, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both PAYEMS and UNRATE increase from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between monthly HOUST and GDPC1 growth signals robust housing and overall demand expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly HOUST and GDPC1 growth is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of positive HOUST and GDPC1 growth correlation.
